sections.h2: Who records deeds in DuPage County
sections.html:
The DuPage County Recorder's Office takes in, reviews, records and keeps every deed, mortgage, lien and plat for property in the county. Its collection reaches back to 1839, the year DuPage was cut out of Cook County.

The office is fee funded, so recording charges pay for its operations. The public line is 630-407-5400 and the research desk answers at 630-407-5401. The counter is open weekdays from 8 a.m. until half past four, and closed on county holidays. Most closings are handled by a company that prepares the deed packet, pays the fees and submits it, so a seller mainly needs to know what gets charged and why.

A standard deed carries an $86.00 filing fee in DuPage County. Nonstandard paper documents cost more, and plats have their own price.

Recording fees for common documents
DocumentRecording fee
Deed (Class 1)$86.00
Lease (Class 2)$86.00
Mortgage (Class 3)$86.00
Easement (Class 4)$86.00
Nonstandard document (Class 5)$112.00
Miscellaneous (Class 7)$86.00
Map or plat (Class 8)$110.00
Military discharge (DD214)No charge

Each fee already includes a $10 document storage charge, a $31 geographic information system charge, a $1 real property charge and an $18 Rental Housing Support Program charge. Copies cost $0.50 a page and a certification costs $5.00 a document. Payment comes with the submission, and the office takes credit cards, checks, money orders and cash. Card payments add a convenience fee: $2.00 on charges of $59.99 or less, and 2.75% on $60.00 or more.

sections.h2: What goes into a deed package
sections.html:
You need a completed deed plus the transfer forms that go with it. The Recorder's Office cannot draft a deed or tell you what your particular document must say, so an attorney or title company handles that part.

A deed package holds these items:

  • The signed deed itself
  • The PTAX form or an exemption statement
  • Municipal transfer stamps, where the village or city requires them
  • A metes and bounds affidavit, if one applies
  • The buyer's name and mailing address for the tax bill
  • The property address and the permanent parcel number from the tax bill
  • The legal description
  • The preparer's name and address

An incomplete document is returned to whoever sent it. A recorded deed is stamped with a number and date, indexed and imaged, then mailed back to the address given, or returned electronically when it came in through eRecording. To change only the name and mailing address on a tax bill, go to the County Clerk.

The state transfer tax is paid with revenue stamps and comes to 50 cents per $500 of value, counting any partial $500 as a full one (35 ILCS 200/31-15). Stamps are sold by the Recorder. Paper stamps ended with 2025, so you now get an electronic stamp or similar proof that the tax was paid.

Every sale also needs a signed Form PTAX-203 real estate transfer declaration. At least one seller and one buyer, or their agents, must sign it. The Illinois Department of Revenue handles questions about the form and the MyDec online tool at 844-445-1114. The DuPage Recorder has accepted MyDec-prepared forms since January 14, 2015.

Some deeds are exempt from the tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-45. The DuPage list includes deeds where the actual consideration is under $100, tax deeds, deeds that only correct or confirm an earlier recorded deed, deeds of partition, and deeds issued to a mortgage holder after foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure. A deed that is exempt under paragraphs (b), (k) or (m) of the county list must still carry a PTAX-203. Local rules sit in the county's Resolution F11879, so ask the Recorder which stamps apply to your deed.

Some DuPage municipalities charge their own transfer stamp and some do not. The Recorder publishes a list of municipal fees and tells owners to contact the village or city before closing, since amounts can change without notice to the office.

  • Elmhurst: $1.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $30.00
  • Addison: $2.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $50.00
  • Wheaton: $2.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $25.00
  • Woodridge: $2.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $25.00
  • Naperville: $3.00 per $1,000, no exemption stamp charge
  • Glen Ellyn: $3.00 per $1,000, no exemption stamp charge
  • Carol Stream: $3.00 per $1,000, exemption stamp $25.00
  • Bolingbrook: $7.50 per $1,000, exemption stamp $50.00

The county list also covers Aurora, Bartlett, Elk Grove, Glendale Heights and Hanover Park. For a town missing from it, ask the village or city hall whether a local stamp applies before closing.

You can. The Recorder accepts deeds, mortgages, releases, liens and similar documents through electronic recording. Plats and DD-214 discharge forms are not accepted that way.

Electronic recording runs through an account with an approved vendor: Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Hopdox, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile. Any setup fee is between the customer and the vendor. Most sellers never open an account, because their closing company already has one.

The other routes are to hand the document in at the office or mail it to the office's mailing address. Documents recorded electronically come back electronically.

sections.h2: How far back the records go
sections.html:
The office keeps records from 1839 to the present. Computer searches cover names from 1961, parcel numbers from 1985 and property addresses from 1995, and plats can be searched back to the 1800s.

Searching and printing images through the online search is free. A copy of a deed shows who owns the property but says nothing about liens, so it is not a substitute for a title search. The office does not run full title searches and carries no errors and omissions coverage, so a title insurance company does that work. A copy of a satisfaction shows that a mortgage was paid off once it has been recorded.

sections.h2: DuPage County for a home seller
sections.html: DuPage County sits west of Chicago and is one of the collar counties of the metro area. The 2025 estimate is 934,298 residents. Wheaton is the county seat and Naperville is the largest city. There are 370,517 housing units, with a 73.1% owner-occupied rate and a median owned-home value of $391,400. Median household income is $112,096 and median gross rent is $1,688.

sections.h2: Property tax around a DuPage County closing
sections.html:
Because bills arrive a year behind, one issued in 2026 pays for tax year 2025. You get a single bill with two coupons, due June 1 and September 1.

Collection is the job of the Treasurer's Office (630-407-5900). It does not set values, so assessment questions belong with the assessor named on the bill. The County Clerk calculates the tax on each parcel and certifies it to the Treasurer. Look for the exemptions listed on the bill, since the general homestead and senior exemptions are $8,000 each. If a mortgage company pays the bill, a yellow box on the bill says so, and a second payment would only create a refund request. The Treasurer reports just under $4 million in such duplicate payments in a recent year.

faqs.q: What does the DuPage County Recorder charge to file a deed?
faqs.a: A standard deed is $86.00, which already covers the storage, GIS, real property and rental housing support charges. Nonstandard documents are $112.00 and plats $110.00. Paying by card adds a convenience fee.

faqs.q: Does the DuPage County Recorder write or review my deed?
faqs.a: No. Staff check that a document meets recording requirements, but they cannot draft a deed or give legal advice. Get the deed from an attorney, title company or form seller. Incomplete packages go back to the sender.

faqs.q: Do I pay Illinois transfer tax if I sell my DuPage County house?
faqs.a: Usually. Revenue stamps at 50 cents per $500 of value are bought when the deed is recorded. A few deeds are exempt under 35 ILCS 200/31-45, for example tax deeds and corrective deeds, and some of those still need a PTAX-203.

faqs.q: Can I look up my deed online for free in DuPage County?
faqs.a: Yes, viewing and printing document images online costs nothing. A deed copy proves ownership but cannot show liens, which need a title search. Copies in person or by mail are $0.50 a page.

faqs.q: Where do I send questions about my DuPage County tax bill?
faqs.a: Payments go through the Treasurer at 630-407-5900, and tax calculation questions go to the County Clerk at 630-407-5500. For the assessed value, call the township assessor on the bill. The Recorder's Office does not handle assessments.
